title: Influence of Diagnosis and Treatment of Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV) in Geriatric Patients: A 10-Year Review (2015–2025)
summary: Falls in the elderly play a significant role and are often the cause of hospital admissions due to fractures, surgical interventions, and subsequent rehabilitation. They frequently lead to a deterioration in quality of life, increased care needs, or admission to a nursing facility. In this context, the nonspecific symptom of dizziness is a common cause of falls. Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV) is a differential diagnosis for dizziness and should be excluded. Epidemiological studies have reported a lifetime prevalence of 2.4%. Affected patients describe a sudden onset of vertigo attacks (usually rotational vertigo) with horizontal nystagmus following rapid head movements or getting out of bed. These vertigo attacks are attributed to the displacement of otoliths in the inner ear, which migrate into the semicircular canals during movement. These attacks typically last for a few seconds and are often accompanied by nausea and vomiting. In the course of repositioning maneuvers, the symptoms are usually fully reversible. Therefore, early diagnosis and appropriate treatment are essential to prevent the complications described.

interventions.name: Investigation of all patients treated for benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV) either inpatient or outpatient at Johanniter Clinics during the observation period from May 2015 to May 2025.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The data were obtained from inpatient and outpatient patients who were treated for benign paroxysmal positional vertigo between May 2015 and May 2025 at the Johanniter Kliniken Bonn, including the Johanniter Krankenhaus Bonn and the Waldkrankenhaus Bonn sites.
Exclusion criteria:
